text: At the Vetra QBR, their director opened by saying he was evaluating competitors. Instead of defending Lumina right away, I spent twenty minutes just mapping what had changed in their operation and brought three of those points to the roadmap meeting the following week. The renewal closed with a plan upgrade.

tags.quote: I spent twenty minutes just mapping what had changed in their operation and brought three of those points to the roadmap meeting

text: I spent Thursday afternoon migrating our accounts from the old master spreadsheet into the new CRM and scheduling the tool trainings for the team. Nothing glamorous, but everything was ready before the end of the day.

Our weekly portfolio meeting kept turning into venting with no conclusions. Juliana set up a fixed three-block agenda, makes it clear who decides what, and closes every topic with an owner and a deadline. These days we leave the room in forty minutes with everything on track.

tags.quote: set up a fixed three-block agenda, makes it clear who decides what, and closes every topic with an owner and a deadline

text: When Juliana missed the deadline to send the Grupo Almeida renewal proposal, she brought it up herself in the team meeting before anyone asked, explained what she was going to change in her process, and asked us to flag it if we ever saw it happening again.

tags.quote: she brought it up herself in the team meeting before anyone asked

text: At the prioritization committee with product, Juliana showed up with recordings of three customers complaining about the export flow and made everyone watch them before opening the backlog. The discussion shifted from opinion to evidence, and the item moved up in priority right there.

tags.quote: showed up with recordings of three customers complaining about the export flow and made everyone watch them before opening the backlog

text: In my first month, I gave TechNorte the wrong contract information and was terrified. Juliana pulled me aside, told me about a similar mistake she had made herself when she was a CSM, and put together the correction email to the client with me. I left that conversation wanting to get it right, not wanting to hide.

tags.quote: told me about a similar mistake she had made herself when she was a CSM
I left that conversation wanting to get it right, not wanting to hide

text: The account handoff between support and CS was a gray area and tickets kept falling into the void. Juliana got both sides into one room, drew the flow on the whiteboard, and only wrapped up once every step had a defined owner. It has been two months without a single ticket getting lost in the transition.

tags.quote: got both sides into one room, drew the flow on the whiteboard, and only wrapped up once every step had a defined owner

text: LogiMax's CFO joined the renewal call already announcing he was going to cancel over the price increase. I let him talk for ten minutes without interrupting, acknowledged point by point what made sense, and proposed revisiting the scope before talking price. We came out with the renewal signed for another twelve months.

tags.quote: I let him talk for ten minutes without interrupting, acknowledged point by point what made sense, and proposed revisiting the scope before talking price

text: After hearing the same complaint about the churn report in two consecutive QBRs, I wrote a summary with the customers' verbatim quotes and took it to the roadmap meeting with product. Two weeks later the fix made it into the quarter's plan.

tags.quote: I wrote a summary with the customers' verbatim quotes and took it to the roadmap meeting with product

text: Last sprint, support and engineering were trading jabs in the channel over who owned the Farmus bug. Otávio pulled the two of them into a quick chat, translated what each side was actually asking for, and the argument died right there, with the fix agreed for Thursday.

tags.quote: pulled the two of them into a quick chat, translated what each side was actually asking for, and the argument died right there

text: When the director at Banco Sollo sent that all-caps email threatening to escalate to the CEO, Otávio asked to join the account with me and replied in a tone that disarmed the client with the very first message. Afterwards he even stayed late reviewing the account's open tickets with me.

tags.quote: replied in a tone that disarmed the client with the very first message
stayed late reviewing the account's open tickets with me

text: I shared a booth with Otávio at the customer event in São Paulo. We took turns during the peak hours, cataloged the lead badges at the end of each day, and still had time to catch two talks from the product track.

During the handover of the Orbita Foods account from sales to CS, the client was upset about promises he felt had not been kept. Otávio ran the transition meeting without pointing fingers at anyone, realigned expectations item by item, and the client ended the call saying thank you.

tags.quote: ran the transition meeting without pointing fingers at anyone, realigned expectations item by item

text: During the billing bug crisis, Otávio personally called each of the eight affected customers before any of them opened a ticket. The next day he even showed up at the support daily asking where he could help clear the queue. Two of the accounts praised Lumina by email after that.

tags.quote: personally called each of the eight affected customers before any of them opened a ticket
showed up at the support daily asking where he could help clear the queue

text: While preparing the ClaraMed QBR, I interviewed four end users on top of the sponsor and discovered the field team didn't even know offline mode existed. I rebuilt the entire presentation around their day-to-day, and the sponsor asked us to repeat the format next quarter.

tags.quote: I interviewed four end users on top of the sponsor

text: When I joined, I was terrified of asking a dumb question in the team channel. Aline made a habit of answering any question of mine by starting with an example of where she herself had once stumbled on the topic. These days I ask anything without thinking twice.

tags.quote: These days I ask anything without thinking twice

text: During the cancellation flow redesign, Aline came in with screenshots of real customer conversations showing exactly where they got stuck, and made us redo two steps that looked great internally. Offboarding NPS went up the following month.

tags.quote: came in with screenshots of real customer conversations showing exactly where they got stuck

text: Aline and I were put in charge of the year-end on-call schedule. We settled the date swaps in one afternoon and sent the calendar out to the team that same week.

I invited Aline to co-facilitate a round of interviews with churned customers. She opened each conversation by acknowledging what Lumina had gotten wrong with that account, and the customers relaxed and shared things that would never show up in a survey.

tags.quote: the customers relaxed and shared things that would never show up in a survey

text: At the quarterly retro, Aline kicked off the conversation about the Farmus churn by first saying what she herself would have done differently, and the whole team dissected the case without anyone getting defensive. Three concrete changes to the onboarding playbook came out of it.

tags.quote: the whole team dissected the case without anyone getting defensive
first saying what she herself would have done differently

text: The TechNorte ticket looked like just an import error, but I kept pulling the thread and found that the integration job had been failing silently since the last update. I wrote up the step-by-step reproduction, opened the incident with engineering, and only marked it resolved after validating the data with the customer.

tags.quote: I kept pulling the thread and found that the integration job had been failing silently since the last update

text: I used the quietest Friday of the month to clean up the old Zendesk macros and update the internal contact list we use to route tickets. Nothing urgent, but it had been sitting in my queue for weeks.

During the payments integration outage, the queue jumped to ninety tickets in an hour and everyone started replying in a scramble. Vítor opened a call, split the queue into three blocks, and dictated the standard response in the same voice you'd use to read a menu. Nobody panicked after that.

tags.quote: dictated the standard response in the same voice you'd use to read a menu
opened a call, split the queue into three blocks

text: My first overnight on-call shift landed right on the migration window that went wrong. I called Vítor at three in the morning thinking it was the end of the world, and he walked me through it step by step, without a hint of irritation in his voice, until the service came back up.

tags.quote: walked me through it step by step, without a hint of irritation in his voice, until the service came back up

text: Banco Sollo had been complaining for months about the dashboard being slow, and the standard answer was that we were monitoring it. Vítor built a load-time comparison on his own initiative, took it to engineering, and followed the case through to the deploy of the fix, updating the client at every step.

tags.quote: built a load-time comparison on his own initiative, took it to engineering, and followed the case through to the deploy of the fix

text: During the database incident, Vítor was our bridge to the customers. While we debugged, he sent updates every twenty minutes in a tone that kept even the most nervous accounts steady, and filtered out the noise so our side could stay focused.

tags.quote: sent updates every twenty minutes in a tone that kept even the most nervous accounts steady

text: When Farmus threatened to cancel over the repeated tickets, Vítor asked to be the single point of contact for the account, mapped the five recurring problems, and closed them out one by one in three weeks, even the ones that depended on other teams. The account renewed without a discount.

tags.quote: asked to be the single point of contact for the account, mapped the five recurring problems, and closed them out one by one in three weeks, even the ones that depended on other teams
closed them out one by one in three weeks

text: I joined knowing nothing about APIs and Orbita Foods kept asking about the integration. I spent two evenings on the internal webhooks course, set up a test environment to practice, and the following week I led the technical call on my own, with on-call just listening in as a safety net.

tags.quote: I spent two evenings on the internal webhooks course, set up a test environment to practice, and the following week I led the technical call on my own

text: The week I had three QBRs piled up, Natália noticed without me saying a word and showed up with the usage-data decks for all three accounts already filled in. All I had to do was review them and record my commentary on top.

tags.quote: noticed without me saying a word and showed up with the usage-data decks for all three accounts already filled in

text: When we migrated the help center to a new tool, Natália was the first to master the new editor. Within two weeks she had already rewritten twenty articles and recorded a short video teaching the rest of the team, without anyone asking.

tags.quote: was the first to master the new editor
recorded a short video teaching the rest of the team, without anyone asking

text: Natália took on collecting the topics for our monthly customer coffee chat and put together the agenda for the next session. It was settled that it will stay in the online format, on the last Thursday of the month.

I was stuck with a list of prospects who had previously been Lumina customers and couldn't figure out their cancellation reasons. Natália, who isn't even on my team, offered to go through them account by account with me during a free hour of her on-call shift and walked me through the history of each one.

tags.quote: offered to go through them account by account with me during a free hour of her on-call shift

text: I gave Natália the most technical account in the portfolio almost as a test. Within a month she absorbed the vocabulary of the logistics sector, rebuilt LogiMax's success plan with metrics that made sense to the client, and switched approaches quickly when the first proposal didn't land.

tags.quote: Within a month she absorbed the vocabulary of the logistics sector

text: I noticed that Vetra's tickets kept coming in with the same manual export request. I called to understand their routine, documented the use case, and brought to the product meeting the numbers on how much time the customer was losing per week because of it.

tags.quote: I called to understand their routine, documented the use case, and brought to the product meeting the numbers on how much time the customer was losing per week

text: This week I updated my email signature to the company's new standard and archived the old folders of closed tickets. While I was at it, I deleted some reply drafts I never got around to using.

We split the legacy ticket migration push and Eduardo nailed it: he promised his four hundred by Friday and delivered Thursday night, with the log of every batch recorded in the spreadsheet. It's the kind of commitment we don't even need to double-check with him.

tags.quote: promised his four hundred by Friday and delivered Thursday night

text: Whenever I promise a customer of mine an update on an escalated ticket, Eduardo is the one on the other end. In the last three ClaraMed cases, he got back to me on the exact date he had agreed with me, including one where he had to chase two other teams to keep the deadline from slipping.

tags.quote: got back to me on the exact date he had agreed with me
had to chase two other teams to keep the deadline from slipping

text: In triage, Eduardo doesn't close a ticket by fixing just the symptom. In the Grupo Almeida case, he picked up from the tone of the messages that the real problem was the client's accounting close, raised the priority, and explained that context to engineering right in the ticket.

tags.quote: picked up from the tone of the messages that the real problem was the client's accounting close

text: I needed usage data for ten accounts for the renewals task force, and Eduardo was the only one who delivered the complete package on the agreed date, even with the support queue slammed that week. I didn't even have to send a reminder.

tags.quote: delivered the complete package on the agreed date, even with the support queue slammed that week

text: On the project to reduce first-response time, Eduardo took on the four-hour target and closed three straight weeks within the goal, adjusting his own shift to cover the hours when retail customers open the most tickets.

tags.quote: closed three straight weeks within the goal
adjusting his own shift to cover the hours when retail customers open the most tickets
